title: Fine-Grained Context Selector with Invalidation Channels
problemStatement: Implement `createContextChannel(initialState)` that supports fine-grained selector subscriptions with custom equality comparators (e.g. shallow array equality).
interviewTrap: Using deep comparison everywhere kills performance. Using `shallowEqual` on array slices avoids unnecessary notification without high diff cost.

testCases.name: Suppresses notifications when shallow array contents match
testCases.input: array slice returns same items with shallow comparison
testCases.testFn: const channel = createContextChannel({ items: [1, 2] }); let notified = 0; const shallowArray = (a, b) => a.length === b.length && a.every((v, i) => v === b[i]); channel.subscribe(s => s.items, () => notified++, shallowArray); channel.emit({ items: [1, 2] }); return notified;

testCases.name: Fires notification when array items differ
testCases.testFn: const channel = createContextChannel({ items: [1, 2] }); let notified = 0; const shallowArray = (a, b) => a.length === b.length && a.every((v, i) => v === b[i]); channel.subscribe(s => s.items, () => notified++, shallowArray); channel.emit({ items: [1, 2, 3] }); return notified;

testCases.name: Maintains independent subscribers across different channels
testCases.input: two subscribers on different state properties
testCases.testFn: const channel = createContextChannel({ a: 1, b: 2 }); let callsA = 0; let callsB = 0; channel.subscribe(s => s.a, () => callsA++); channel.subscribe(s => s.b, () => callsB++); channel.emit({ a: 99 }); return [callsA, callsB];

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: When a Context Provider's `value` prop changes identity, EVERY component that calls `useContext(MyContext)` MUST re-render, bypassing any `React.memo` or `shouldComponentUpdate` checks. Splitting into separate `StateContext` and `DispatchContext` prevents dispatch consumers from re-rendering on state changes.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for Zustand-Style Subscription Architecture.
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React Fiber, Zustand-Style Subscription Architecture maintains state across work-in-progress trees and lanes scheduling priority.

complexity.time: O(1) per hook / O(N) fiber traversal

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How do external selector stores (Zustand / Redux) achieve fine-grained invalidation compared to React Context?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: They move state management outside of React's reconciler! The store is a plain JavaScript object maintaining a `Set` of listener callbacks. When state updates, the store iterates listeners, evaluates each subscriber's selector (`state => state.field`), and uses `Object.is` to compare with the previous slice. If equal, it does nothing; if changed, it calls the listener to trigger a targeted update via `useSyncExternalStore`.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: High-level state management architecture interview question.

realWorldUseCases.description: Managing thousands of dynamic state properties in 3D canvas and canvas editors with zero context re-renders.

howToExplain.opening: Fine-grained selector stores achieve O(1) targeted re-renders by moving state outside React and notifying only components whose selected slices fail equality checks.
keyPoints: State lives in an external JS store outside React Context.
Only components with changed slices re-render.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Selector stores solve the context performance dilemma by decoupling state storage from component tree hierarchy.
analogies: A pager system: instead of shouting over a megaphone to the entire room (context), only the doctor whose pager buzzes (subscriber) stands up.

commonMistakes.mistake: Selecting the entire store state: const state = useStore(state => state).
commonMistakes.why: Defeats all fine-grained optimizations by re-rendering on every state change.
commonMistakes.correct: Always select the smallest slice needed: `useStore(s => s.user.name)`.

followUpDeepDive.question: How does useSyncExternalStore prevent infinite re-render loops with non-primitive selectors?
followUpDeepDive.answer: `useSyncExternalStore` relies on `Object.is(getSnapshot(), prevSnapshot)`. If a selector returns a new object reference every time (`state => ({ a: state.a })`), React detects an unstable snapshot and throws a Maximum update depth exceeded error.
